questions.question: Why was the year 1757 an important year for the English East India Company in India?
questions.option_1: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Madras by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
questions.option_2: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Oudh by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Berar.
questions.option_3: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Bengal by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
questions.option_4: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Hyderabad by defeating the Nizam in the Battle of Plassey.
questions.solution:
The year 1757 is crucial because of the Battle of Plassey, where the British defeated Siraj-ud-daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.
  • This victory gave the East India Company a firm foothold and political influence in Bengal.
  • Robert Clive led the British forces in this battle.

questions.question: Whose prashasti was found on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad?
questions.solution:
The Prayag Prashasti, found on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad, contains an account of the conquests of Samudragupta.
  • It was composed by his court poet Harishena.
  • It provides a detailed list of the kings and regions defeated by him.

questions.question: The second round table conference was held in ______.
questions.solution:
The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in December 1931.
  • Mahatma Gandhi attended as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
  • The conference failed due to disagreements over communal electorates.

questions.question: _________ and ___________ formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress to argue for a return to council politics.
questions.solution:
Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in 1923.
  • They wanted to contest elections and enter the legislative councils to oppose British policies from within.
  • This was a response to the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.question: How many rulers of Dakshinapatha were defeated by Samudragupta?
questions.solution:
Samudragupta is said to have defeated 12 rulers of Dakshinapatha (South India).
  • Unlike his policy in North India, he reinstated these kings as tributaries after their surrender.
  • This policy is described as Grahana-Moksha-Anugraha.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is named only once in Rigveda?
questions.solution:
The Ganga river is mentioned only once in the Rigveda.
  • The Saraswati was considered the holiest river, while the Indus (Sindhu) was mentioned most frequently.
  • This suggests the Aryans were primarily settled in the Sapta-Sindhu region during the early Vedic period.

questions.question: Which of the following major incidents occurred in 1919?
questions.solution:
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre is the major incident that occurred in 1919.
  • It was a direct consequence of the repressive Rowlatt Act.
  • Rabindranath Tagore returned his Knighthood in protest against this massacre.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan emperors was known by the name of Piyadassi?
questions.solution:
The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka was also referred to as Piyadassi (He who looks with kindness) and Devanampiya (Beloved of the gods).
  • These titles are found in his numerous inscriptions across the Indian subcontinent.
  • He was the first ruler to communicate directly with his subjects through inscriptions.

questions.question: In 1873, he founded the Satya-Shodhak Samaj. Who is referred to as 'he' here?
questions.solution:
In 1873, Jyotiba Phule founded the Satya-Shodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers).
  • The organization aimed to liberate the oppressed castes and promote education for women.
  • He wrote the famous book 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery).

questions.question: Who among the following was the court poet of Harshavardhana and the author of ‘Harshacharita’?
questions.solution:
Banabhatta was the court poet of King Harshavardhana and wrote his biography, 'Harshacharita'.
  • He also wrote 'Kadambari', one of the world's earliest novels.
  • 'Harshacharita' provides valuable information about the administration and society during Harsha's time.

questions.question: In 1866, who among the following founded the East India Association in London?
questions.solution:
Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in 1866.
  • The goal was to inform the British public and Parliament about the grievances of Indians.
  • He was also the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons.

questions.question: On the banks of which river was the war between Harshavardhana and Pulakeshin II fought?
questions.solution:
The battle between Harshavardhana and Pulakeshin II was fought on the banks of the Narmada river.
  • Harsha was defeated, which checked his expansion into the Deccan.
  • This event is recorded in the Aihole Inscription.

questions.question: The concepts of Dhamma was popularized by which of the following Mauryan kings?
questions.solution:
The concept of Dhamma was popularized by the Mauryan King Ashoka.
  • It was not a religion but a code of conduct and social ethics.
  • He appointed Dhamma Mahamattas to spread these principles.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Vakataka Dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Vakataka Dynasty was founded by Vindhyashakti in the 3rd century AD.
  • The dynasty was a contemporary of the Guptas.
  • They were famous patrons of the Ajanta Caves.

questions.question: In 1928, the _____ was founded at a meeting in Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi. Amongst its leaders were Bhagat Singh, Jatin Das and Ajoy Ghosh.
questions.solution:
The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.
  • Key leaders included Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and Rajguru.
  • The organization aimed for a revolution against British rule and the establishment of a socialist state.

questions.question: Ashoka mentioned in his inscription that he conquered Kalinga _________ after he became the king.
questions.solution:
Ashoka's inscriptions state that he conquered Kalinga eight years after his coronation.
  • This occurred around 261 BC.
  • The war is described as having caused immense suffering to both civilians and soldiers.

questions.question: In 1919, Gandhiji called for satyagraha against the _________.
questions.solution:
In 1919, Gandhi organized a Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act.
  • It was the first 'All India' political agitation under his leadership.
  • The Act was dubbed the 'Black Act' because it denied the right to 'Vakil, Dalil, or Appeal'.

questions.question: According to the Chola inscriptions, what was the land for the maintenance of a schools called?
questions.solution:
According to Chola inscriptions, Shalabhoga was land donated for the maintenance of a school.
  • Brahmadeya was land gifted to Brahmins.
  • Devadana was land gifted to temples.

questions.question: In which year was the Depressed Classes Association established by B. R. Ambedkar?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar established the Depressed Classes Association in 1930.
  • He represented the interests of Dalits at the Round Table Conferences.
  • He demanded separate electorates for the depressed classes.
  • The association was formed to organize and uplift the community.

questions.question: Rajagriha was the capital of Magadha for several years. Later the capital was shifted to ______.
questions.solution:
The capital of Magadha was later shifted from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.
  • King Udayin is credited with founding the new city at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers.
  • Pataliputra remained a major political center for centuries under the Mauryas and Guptas.

questions.question: Ghiyasuddin Balban ruled in India in which of the following period?
questions.solution:
Ghiyasuddin Balban, a powerful Sultan of the Slave Dynasty, ruled from 1266 to 1287.
  • He introduced the Persian customs of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the king's feet).
  • He followed a policy of 'Blood and Iron' to consolidate the empire.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January ______.
questions.solution:
The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement officially began in January 1921.
  • It saw massive participation from students, lawyers, and common citizens.
  • It combined the Indian nationalist struggle with the grievances of the Muslim community regarding the Caliphate.

questions.question: Nalanda University was established by __________ in the 5th century.
questions.solution:
Nalanda University was established during the 5th century by the Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I.
  • It became a world-renowned center for Buddhist learning.
  • It was later destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji in the late 12th century.

questions.question: Which of the following was the main argument put forward by the British for the partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.solution:
The British officially argued that the Partition of Bengal was for administrative convenience.
  • However, the real motive was to 'divide and rule' by creating a rift between Hindus and Muslims.
  • The move led to the massive Anti-Partition or Swadeshi Movement.

questions.question: The Satavahana kingdom was established about how many years ago?
questions.solution:
The Satavahana kingdom was established approximately 2,100 years ago (around the 1st century BC).
  • They were also known as the Andhras.
  • Prominent rulers included Gautamiputra Satakarni.
